resources.string: In the Settings menu, you can set which sounds you\'d like to receive with TestProduct notifications.
Be aware that putting your phone on Silent Mode or Do Not Disturb will also silence TestProduct notifications.
Settings also allows you to set a time to be notified with an alarm that does bypass Do Not Disturb settings – ideal for sleeping.
You now know the basics of using the TestProduct app. You can revisit this tour and explore other helpful information in Guides, accessed through the app\'s main menu.
TestProduct will keep you informed of any signs of leakage.
An introduction to all the basics of using the TestProduct app.
Your Status screen is the app\'s main screen. It shows the status of your baseplate. You\'ll receive notifications if leakage is detected.
If the inner sensors on your sensor layer detect signs of leakage, you\'ll be notified and see this message.
If leakage makes it to the outer sensors, you\'ll be notified again and see this message.
By pressing on the sensor symbol on your Status screen you can open a detailed view to see the direction and spread of any leakage.
You can see the battery level of your attached transmitter in the bottom left corner of your status screen.
The app\'s main menu is opened in the top right corner. Here you can access things like Guides and Settings.
The Guides menu has everything you need to know about TestProduct, including how to reapply during your next change.
A step-by-step guide to applying a new sensor layer and attaching your transmitter
It\'s recommended that you use the Applying guide when changing your product, at least for the first times.
When your transmitter is attached to a sensor layer, you can see its current battery level in the bottom right corner of the Status screen.
View attached transmitter battery level on Status screen

In Transmitters, you can see the transmitters you have in range of your smartphone. You can see the battery level for the transmitter you have attached to a sensor layer. You will also be able to see an estimated battery level for any transmitter in range, but not attached to a sensor layer.
View unattached transmitter battery level estimate in Transmitters
How to check the battery level of your transmitter

Your transmitter relies on Bluetooth to communicate with your smartphone. This means that you need to keep your phone's Bluetooth turned on and to keep your phone nearby to stay informed.

Bluetooth connection can be disrupted by distance, thick walls, or the presence of too many other Bluetooth connected devices.

In the top left corner of your Status screen there is a bluetooth symbol. The symbol is turquoise when your phone and transmitter are connected. The symbol is grey if connection is lost.

When your transmitter loses connection, it has the ability to broadcast its location to your smartphone, so that they can reconnect automatically when they come back into range.

To ensure the most reliable connection to keep you informed, it is recommended to set location access for TestProduct to 'Always' in your phones settings.

To read more about how TestProduct uses location data and what to do with reoccuring popups asking for you to confirm your location preference, you may wish to read the Location guide:
Allowing location access can help improve your connection
Tips for keeping TestProduct connected to stay informed

Place the transmitter into the cradle of the charger. Insert the supplied cable into the charger. Insert the other end of the cable into a USB power plug – for example, like the one you normally use to charge your phone – and connect to power.

When the status light is blinking, the transmitter is charging. When the status light is constantly on, the transmitter is fully charged. When the status light is off, the charger is not connected to power.

You can charge your transmitter fully within 3 hours. A full charge will last about 2 days.
Everything you need to know about charging your transmitter
It is important to keep your transmitter and charger clean so that they function properly.

Disengage your transmitter lid by pulling the lid firmly until it is opened up. You should be able to see the metal connector pins inside the transmitter.

Clean the transmitter regularly using a soft cloth. You can clean it using water or cleaning agents like mild soap or alcohol. 

Wipe the transmitter with a dry cloth after cleaning, making sure the metal connector pins, lid and sides (inside and outside) are completely dry. 

Remember to close the disengaged lid fully, before attempting attaching again.

For more on drying your transmitter, take a look at the Drying guide:
You can clean your charger using a dry cloth. \n\nDo not use water or cleaning agents.
Everything you need to know about cleaning all the parts of your TestProduct system

If your baseplate and/or sensor layer adhesive becomes wet during application you may experience poor adhesion to the skin, and TestProduct may not be able to detect leakage effectively.

Make sure you carefully wipe both your ostomy and surrounding skin dry immediately before applying a new baseplate/adhesive with sensor layer attached. 

Make sure your supporting products are completely dry before attaching your baseplate/adhesive.

Try not to touch the ostomy with the centre hole of the baseplate/adhesive whilst applying to the body.
Dry application of TestProduct is essential to enable leak detection.
Keeping skin and product dry will give you the best TestProduct experience

If the connection between your transmitter and sensor layer connector flap becomes wet, TestProduct may struggle to keep you informed. It is important to dry these parts when needed, for example, after showering.

It is recommended to remove your transmitter before swimming. You may leave it on for showering/bathing but you should dry out the transmitter (and sensor layer – see below) afterwards.
To dry off your transmitter, first disengage the lid by pulling the lid firmly until it is opened up. You should be able to see the metal connector pins inside the transmitter.
Dry the transmitter using a soft cloth. Make sure the metal connector pins, lid and sides (inside and outside) are completely dry before attempting to attach to a sensor layer.
Remember to close the disengaged lid fully (so the lid is level with the surface of the transmitter) before proceeding to lift the lid to a fixed, lifted position for attaching.

After showering, bathing or swimming, thoroughly dry the connector flap on your sensor layer before reattaching your transmitter. \n\nPlace a thin cotton cloth or absorbing paper (e.g. toilet paper or kitchen paper towel) between the white flap and the sensor layer and press down. This will ensure that any moisture is removed.
Everything you need to know about drying your transmitter and sensor layer
If your transmitter is lost or broken beyond repair, you may need to delete it from your account before you can add another one.
In Transmitters, identify which transmitter you\'d like to delete. Then, press \'Edit\'. Alternatively, swipe the transmitter to the left.
Press \'Delete\' next to the transmitter you would like to delete. Confirm when prompted.
If your transmitter is lost or broken, this simple guide shows you how to delete it

More information on why TestProduct needs location access
Why TestProduct needs location access and what to do with your phone\'s location pop-ups
Location access allows your phone and transmitter to keep you connected with minimal fuss, despite the inevitable disturbances of daily life.
If you and your transmitter move too far away from your phone (for example, when taking the bins out), connection can be lost.
However, if desconnected, your transmitter can broadcast it\'s location to your phone so they can reconnect automatically when back in range.
During setup, you turned location access \'On\' to allow your phone and transmitter to connect.
During setup, you learned it is recommended that you set location access to allow \'Always\' in your phones settings, to ensure connection.
TestProduct will not track or record your location at any time. Location is used for reconnection purposes only.
From time to time, yout phone will ask you to confirm your location permissions and may show a map of where your location has been used.
As location use is not continuous and only used for reconnection, this should have minimal drain on your phone battery.
The map shows where location data was used to reconnect your phone and transmitter. Coloplast will never actively track or record your location.
Will it drain my phone battery?

Place the sensor layer on a flat surface. Identify its connector flap and lift it firmly upwards. This prepares it for attaching your transmitter later.
